etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Borrowed from Latin obiūrgātus, perfect passive participle of obiūrgō (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from ob- (“to, against”) +‎ iūrgō (“to dispute, chide”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵeti.
senses: (intransitive) To remonstrate, complain, to rail against. [1642]
